minutes.headline: Sewer Commission wants state, attorney and owner input on an illegal Mass Ave connection before setting a fine.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was about an unpermitted, uninspected sewer connection at 384 Mass Ave. Members favored the regulation's fine but chose to hear from the state, consult the attorney and invite the owner and contractor in January. They also agreed how to review the maintenance plan, approved the Q2 commitment and the 11/16 minutes, and heard business manager reports.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; nobody was present or raising a hand.

votes.motion: Approve the second quarter sewer commitment and warrant dated November 23rd

budget_items.topic: Fine for illegal connection at 384 Mass Ave
budget_items.what_was_said: Members read the regulation as setting a minimum fine, possibly per day, and discussed leaving the amount open pending further costs. Legal and other costs are to be tracked and charged back to the contractor.
Business manager sought approval of the Q2 billing commitment and warrant covering quarterly billing and adjustments.
A first debt service invoice from Leominster is expected and relates to FY21 payment despite referencing FY20.
figures_as_heard: thirty thousand eight thirty four oh five

budget_items.what_was_said: Price quoted for the year; an agreement is being worked out and is about half the prior price because staff do minor maintenance.
Fitchburg invoice was lower because of drought; Leominster invoice is based on flows.
Participants in the deduct meter program have been billed the fee on the Q2 invoices.
Letters went out; if unpaid in 30 days they will be liened to tax bills.
Members said next year's budget must include money for the maintenance plan, including jetting.

decisions.decision: Wait to hear from the state, talk to the attorney, invite the owner and contractor to the January meeting, and be prepared to impose the fine.
Business manager will raise the matter with counsel at council hours next Wednesday.
Rob has the commission's backing to do what is needed, including possibly a survey, and to track costs for back-charging.
Members will send maintenance plan comments to Rob; Rob will compile them, with review resuming in January.
Seek a written statement from the former DPW director through the attorney.
Send lunch (pizza) to the water department for its new building from the sewer commission.
Next meetings set for January 12, 2021 and January 26 at five o'clock.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission took no vote on a fine for an unpermitted, uninspected sewer connection at 384 Mass Ave, and chose to gather input first.
Members favored the regulation's fine and agreed to hear from the state, consult the attorney, and invite the owner and contractor in January.
The business manager will raise the matter with counsel next Wednesday, and the commission backed tracking costs, possibly including a survey, for back-charging.
Members will send maintenance plan comments to Rob, who will compile them, with review resuming in January.
The commission approved the second quarter sewer commitment and warrant dated November 23rd.

why_it_matters: The outcome of the 384 Mass Ave matter decides whether the cost of an illegal connection falls on the contractor or on sewer ratepayers.
Members said next year's budget must include money for the maintenance plan, including jetting, so it may affect future sewer bills.
watch_next: Sewer Commission meetings on January 12, 2021 and January 26 at five o'clock, with the owner and contractor invited to January.
Advice from the state and the attorney, and a written statement from the former DPW director sought through the attorney.
